Definition: exile, concretely, prisoners; figuratively, a former state of prosperity
BiblicalUsage: Captivity is the state of a people carried away, and this word almost always comes with its reversal. Amos hears that God will bring again the captivity of His people, Jeremiah hears it for Israel and Judah and even for Moab, and Zephaniah hears it as a promise before their eyes: when I turn back your captivity, I will make you a name and a praise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the turning is the heart of the word. Captivity is real, and exile is long, but God brings His people again, and I hold that no captivity is beyond His turning.
